title: Geometrical Tree - Leaf mass & leaf-tree relationship

limitations: All 29 pages were rendered at 150 DPI and visually reviewed through five contact sheets and selected full-resolution equation pages.
The source has complete text coverage, but several mathematical glyphs on pages 17-19 required visual transcription.
Equation 3 on page 18 is recorded at medium transcription confidence because small subscripts and grouped factors are difficult to distinguish.
No blank, clipped, overlapping, or missing rendered content was found.

deliverables: Construct a geometric representation of a tree crown and leaf distribution.
Model sunlight irradiance inside the crown.
Investigate whether observed leaf shape relates to tree profile through sunlight exposure.
Estimate total leaf mass and explore its relation with tree size.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: The official problem statement was not used in this transaction; deliverables are reconstructed from the paper.

section_map.summary: Four-band target-model-application summary with one explicit leaf-size boundary and one limited-data caveat.
Two foundational models, two applications, improvement, conclusion, letter, references, and MATLAB appendix.
Two targets, two model roles, and two applications in body order.
Paracladial geometry, terminal leaves, straight light, irradiance-only photosynthesis, sufficient nutrients, and negligible disturbance.
Four-class leaf decision tree based on convexity, leaf index, and longest-width position.
Recursive branch transformations and stochastic leaf placement.
Annual sky brightness and Monsi-Saeki crown attenuation.
Directional shadow exposure metric and four-shape ranking.
Photosynthesis, venation-LMA relations, LAI accounting, and case study.
Visual geometry selection and one total-leaf-mass estimate.
Exploratory pooled and profile-specific simulation regressions.
Large-leaf discretization, omitted photosynthesis drivers, and two broad conclusions.
Binary branch generation and grid-based projected-area routines.

contributions.summary: Separates two foundational models from two downstream applications and carries a major size-dependent failure boundary onto the first page.
Provides a complete body-order dependency roadmap from geometry and irradiance to leaf-shape comparison and total mass.
Encodes parent-child branch geometry with a local rotation-scaling matrix and endpoint recursion.
Connects crown path length to a directional irradiance integral.
Defines a normalized sky-weighted shadow metric for finite leaf-shape comparison.
Makes local irradiance an explicit input to net photosynthesis.
Ends the multiscale chain with total leaf mass equal to weighted LMA times LAI-scaled crown area.
Publishes the main branch-generation and projection code, enabling equation-code parity inspection.

edges: branch endpoints -> terminal branches -> leaf positions
crown and leaf geometry -> directional path length -> point irradiance
sky brightness plus leaf shadows -> weighted exposure score -> selected shape
point irradiance -> net photosynthesis -> individual LMA
individual LMA plus projected crown area plus LAI -> total leaf mass
feedbacks: leaf placement uses irradiance through d(I) and p(I), while irradiance depends on the generated leaf placement
dependency_graph.closure_status: The high-level sequence is explicit, but d(I), p(I), the sunlight angular measure, the photosynthesis root, LMA weighting, and case-tree validation remain unclosed.

assumptions.summary: Subbranches preserve the structural characteristics of their parent apart from size.
Most leaves grow on the last branch generation.
Light travels in straight lines and diffraction and refraction are ignored.
Photosynthesis varies only with sunlight irradiance while CO2 is homogeneous across the crown.
Moonlight, artificial light, destructive environmental effects, and nutrient limitations are negligible.
The leaf-spacing response is represented by an unexplained N(0.1,0.1) assumption.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: A 0.5 cm grid approximates leaf polygons before convexity, index, and D/L threshold classification.
Leaf index 3.5 and D/L intervals [1/4,3/4] define four shape classes.
Three simulated crown profiles and four candidate leaf classes form the shape-ranking cases.
Field rays produce 32 possible local coordinate systems and a visually selected crown; leaf dimensions come from a manual.
Ground area 6.001436 m^2, LAI 12, and reported LMA around 177.7 g/m^2 feed the case result.
Thirty simulated cases across three crown profiles form pooled and stratified plots.

models.summary: MU-A-2012-15065-001: recursive 3D branch geometry, 6 source equations.
MU-A-2012-15065-002: phyllotaxis and irradiance-linked placement, 1 set equation with two omitted response functions.
MU-A-2012-15065-003: sky discretization and crown attenuation, 3 equations.
MU-A-2012-15065-004: directional shadow scoring and finite shape selection, 4 equations.
MU-A-2012-15065-005: light-response and CO2-diffusion algebra, 5 equations.
MU-A-2012-15065-006: venation-LMA and LAI mass synthesis, 6 equations.

verification.summary: Three worked profiles select the depicted real leaf class among four candidates, without holdout, tolerance, or uncertainty.
Thirty-two coordinate systems are reduced by visual similarity rather than a calibration loss.
The reported 12777.84 g is not compared with observed total leaf mass.
Thirty simulated cases show weak pooled and stronger stratified trends, not observed-tree validation.
The paper acknowledges that large leaves collapse shape discrimination under the grid algorithm.
The code projects branch points rather than explicit leaf polygons, challenging the body definition of SE.

results_trace.summary: The highest score matches the displayed pine, poplar, and Japanese banana leaf classes in three finite tests.
Japanese banana scores 0.83 and 0.85 for two shapes, exposing weak separation.
Ground area, LAI, and LMA produce a reported 12777.84 g leaf-mass prediction.
Profile-specific simulated mass appears to increase approximately cubically with height, subject to limited data.

writing_logic.summary: Target -> two-model architecture -> leaf-shape method/result/boundary -> leaf-mass method/case/data boundary.
The first paragraph compresses the complete dependency chain into body order.
Two model bullets and two application bullets make model roles and reuse explicit.
Hypothesis -> held-structure comparison -> exposure metric -> finite argmax -> observed-shape comparison.
Local irradiance -> photosynthesis -> venation LMA -> weighted LMA -> projected area -> total mass.
Each paragraph names an omitted feature or failure regime before a possible extension, but not an implementation.
Findings precede contributions for a broad audience, but validation boundaries are weakened.

language_observations.summary: The Summary uses a repeatable target-model-application-result-boundary sequence and supplies the third independent source for LP-A-ABS-PARAGRAPH-CHAIN after broadening its final move to decision or scientific meaning.
A held-fixed structure, three candidates, common metric, observed comparator, result, and large-leaf boundary independently support LP-A-ABS-TASK-METHOD-RESULT and LP-A-ABS-BOUNDARY.
Vector-tree geometry and sunlight irradiance are complementary models; they do not support LP-A-ABS-MODEL-STAIRCASE.
Accurate enough, real-life data, generally maximize, and good for require metrics, provenance, counts, and thresholds.
The opening paragraph names both targets and the two foundational states before previewing the two applications.
The explicit two-model/two-application outline raises LP-A-INT-METHOD-ROADMAP to five independent papers.
Given -> Then -> Thus -> Finally is effective because each move consumes a named upstream output.
The phrase proves insight conflicts with the immediate call for a larger sample; the boundary should precede the interpretation.
However and Thus connect a large-leaf failure symptom to an improvement target, but the replacement algorithm is absent.
The letter foregrounds findings and a named SE metric but strengthens claims beyond the body evidence.

visualization_observations.summary: Local coordinate diagrams sit beside the transformation matrix, making theta and phi physically interpretable.
Overhead and oblique 3D views connect sun direction to projected crown points, but leaf polygons, union area, scale, and metric region are not shown.
A compact table aligns three tree profiles, candidate scores, chosen shape, and observed shape; score uncertainty is absent.
Four small scatter plots lack fitted equations, uncertainty, residuals, readable labels, and simulated-data status.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The explicit architecture and front-page boundary improve traceability and claim calibration; no judge source proves a causal score effect.
A body-order dependency map may reduce reviewer search cost; judge relevance remains correlational and unverified.
Publishing executable code improves auditability, while code-body mismatches can also expose unsupported results.

weaknesses.summary: d(I) and p(I) are absent and create an unresolved geometry-light feedback loop.
The phi definition and printed angular weight are inconsistent and can generate negative directional weights.
The printed root does not solve the preceding quadratic.
The per-leaf weighting rule and physiological parameters are absent.
The LMA value changes from 177.74 to 177.47 and no observed total leaf mass is supplied.
The code counts projected branch points rather than explicit leaf-shadow polygons.

independent_extensions.summary: Initialize leaf placement from species priors, solve irradiance, update d(I) and p(I), and iterate to a documented fixed-point tolerance with nonnegative spacing.
Replace summed individual shadow areas with a polygon-union or alpha-coverage estimator and validate angular and grid convergence.
Re-derive and substitute all roots, enforce biological domains, and calibrate parameters from measured leaf gas exchange.
Measure case-tree LAI and harvested or allometric leaf mass, then propagate geometry, physiology, LAI, and LMA uncertainty.

candidate_rule_impacts.basis: Summary and conclusion show both effective boundaries and unsupported adequacy, optimality, and proof wording.
The outline, transformation diagrams, summary, and letter provide layered explanation but weaken evidence in audience prose.
The body-order roadmap is strong while several later interfaces fail closure.
Geometry, irradiance, physiology, LMA, LAI, and mass form a visible multiscale chain with missing typed interfaces.
Missing d(I), p(I), a feedback solve, angular consistency, and a valid quadratic root block implementation.
Three shape matches and one mass case are worked examples rather than independent validation.
Code is published, but equation-code objects, root algebra, and case values do not remain identical.
The appendix acts as a second specification and reveals that usefulArea counts points rather than leaf polygons.
Mechanism diagrams aid interpretation while result figures omit uncertainty and residual evidence.
Measured, visually selected, literature-transferred, and assumed case inputs are not separated with uncertainty.

unresolved_questions: What rounding operation is intended by N=[theta sigma(k)]?
What are the functional forms, domains, and calibration data for d(I) and p(I)?
How is the leaf-placement and irradiance feedback solved?
What is the correct spherical coordinate convention and angular measure?
What is the corrected quadratic solution for net photosynthesis?
What values are used for m, venation traits, stomatal traits, and physiological parameters?
How are per-leaf LMA values weighted?
Was LAI measured for the case tree or transferred only from literature?
Is the intended case LMA 177.74 or 177.47 g/m^2?
What observed total leaf mass supports the 12777.84 g claim?
Does usefulArea intend to count branch points, leaf centers, or actual leaf polygons?
